appraisal_events.evidence: "C'est vrai que je n'avais pas été à la Maison Dorée, que je sortais de chez Forcheville... Je t'ai dit que je venais de la Maison d'Or parce que j'avais peur que cela ne t'ennuie"; "un être vicieux, affectant toujours la même vertu devant les êtres de qui il ne veut pas que soient soupçonnés ses vices"
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette is shown, in her own admissions and in narratorial commentary, to have repeatedly lied to Swann about her whereabouts and companions, undermining her credibility independently of Swann's own suffering.

status_effects.explanation: Her exposed pattern of casual lying (about the Maison Dorée, Forcheville, and excuses given to Mme Verdurin) diminishes her reliability as a narrated figure, though the passage remains largely filtered through Swann's jealous perception.

ambiguities: Swann's opening question references a prior suspicion about Odette and Mme Verdurin, but Odette's confession instead locates the remembered incident with an unnamed woman at the Bois; Mme Verdurin's involvement is neither confirmed nor given a distinct local outcome in this passage, so she was left unscored.

Much of the passage's characterization of Odette's dishonesty is filtered through Swann's jealousy-heightened perception, so the degree to which the narrator independently endorses this diminishment (versus reporting Swann's subjective torment) is somewhat uncertain.
